hero.headline: Palm Beach County man leads Martin County deputies on 100 mph chase through Indiantown
hero.body:
A Palm Beach County man led Martin County deputies on a high-speed chase through Indiantown after driving more than 100 mph on State Road 710, one of the area's most dangerous roads. Deputies spotted 33-year-old Markell Tillman driving aggressively at speeds exceeding 100 mph, forcing other vehicles off the roadway. When deputies attempted to stop him, Tillman fled.

Tillman weaved through traffic in an attempt to lose deputies before turning onto SW Martin Highway toward Palm City, where he continued to drive recklessly. Deputies spotted Tillman again traveling eastbound on Martin Highway near Allapattah Road. Deputies used stop sticks to disable his vehicle near I-95.

Tillman then bailed out of the vehicle and attempted to flee on foot before deputies caught up with him and took him into custody. He was arrested on multiple charges including fleeing and eluding, aggravated fleeing with injury or damage, operating a vehicle exceeding the speed limit by 50 or more mph, driving while license suspended or revoked, obstruction without violence, and operating a vehicle at 100 or more mph.

Tillman also had an out-of-county warrant at the time of his arrest. He was booked into the Martin County Jail.

cards.headline: Argentina rallies past England 2-1 with late goals to reach World Cup final
cards.teaser: Argentina scored two goals in the final minutes to defeat England 2-1 in the World Cup semifinals. The defending champions will face Spain in the final Sunday in East Rutherford, New Jersey.
cards.body:
Argentina scored two goals in the final minutes to defeat England 2-1 on Wednesday in the World Cup semifinals. Trailing 1-0 going into the 85th minute, Enzo Fernandez swept in the equalizer from outside the box after receiving a pass from Lionel Messi. Two minutes into stoppage time, Messi sent in a cross for substitute Lautaro Martinez to head in the winner. Martinez said he had told Alexis Mac Allister before the match that he was going to come on and win it. The defending champions will take on European champion Spain in the final on Sunday in East Rutherford, New Jersey.

England took the lead when Anthony Gordon scored in the 55th minute but could not hold on as Argentina mounted wave after wave of attacks. England goalkeeper Jordon Pickford made vital saves and Mac Allister sent a header off the post as the English held on. England captain Harry Kane said he was gutted for the team, staff and fans, saying the players gave every bit of blood, sweat and tears but falling short was gutting. The loss marks the third time England has fallen in the World Cup semifinals after losses to Germany in 1990 and Croatia in 2018. Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni said the team proved its collectiveness and brotherhood, noting they were ready to go home sad but proved themselves after England scored.

cards.headline: Flip City Gym and Cheer gymnasts finish top 15 at nationals, qualify for Junior Olympics
cards.body:
Three young gymnasts from Flip City Gym and Cheer secured a top 15 finish at AAU Nationals in Knoxville, Tennessee last month and qualified for the Junior Olympics in Iowa next month. Skylar Rose-Daris, Victoria Supan, and Charli Rine competed as a unit on the national stage after finding their way to gymnastics through different paths.

Head Coach Candice Lazuka described the season as strong, with the team competing locally and traveling before advancing to states and regionals. At AAU Nationals in Knoxville, the gymnasts came close to a perfect score. Lazuka said the team scored a 9.9, noting that a perfect 10 is hard to achieve.

The top 15 finish qualified the team for the Junior Olympics in Iowa next month. Rose-Daris said it will be really fun to go to an entire different part of the world. Supan described the feeling as happy and exciting at the same time.

Rine said she is focused on getting first place on floors heading into the Junior Olympics. The gymnasts each came to the sport for different reasons, with Rose-Daris citing her ability to do a cartwheel, Supan inspired by gymnasts she saw on YouTube, and Rine loving to learn new things.

cards.headline: Villa Del Sol residents return home after nearly 2 years following structural damage in St. Lucie County
cards.body:
Villa Del Sol residents in St. Lucie County are returning home after nearly two years of displacement from their condos. Residents were notified last month they could return after an inspection in August 2024 found structural damage in buildings 3, 4, and 5, which were deemed unsafe. WPTV received emails sent to residents from the Board of Directors telling them they could return. WPTV also obtained a letter from engineers sent to St. Lucie County's Building Department requesting they lift occupancy restrictions following their special inspection.

Katie Johnson was the first to share with WPTV that residents had been told they could come back. She said she almost didn't believe it and that it was like too good to be true. Johnson described the work still underway at the property, noting that crews are still moving dirt back under the buildings. She reflected on the effort required to bring residents home, saying it's hard work. Johnson also said she is thinking of neighbors who cannot return and feels bad that some were hit harder than others with the situation.

Robert Segedin took WPTV inside his family's home and said he was excited to return but was thinking about those who cannot. He said their hearts were broken and they wanted to spend the rest of their lives at Villa Del Sol. Eric Johnson is among those not coming back. He was one of the first residents WPTV met at Villa Del Sol and is now living in Georgia. He said it's been a terrible two years and the financial toll has been severe.

Eric Johnson said his family had to drain all their savings accounts and 401ks just trying to make ends meet while this was going on. He is filing for bankruptcy and filing his condo for foreclosure. He said it's been a real struggle and that while he'd like to say they are finally starting to climb out of it, it still feels like they're kind of still falling and waiting to start climbing back up. The displaced residents have faced significant financial hardship during their time away from their homes, though some are now able to move back into the property.

cards.headline: Safe Kids Treasure Coast offers free pool alarms to Martin County residents
cards.teaser: The Florida Department of Health and Safe Kids Treasure Coast are providing a limited supply of free pool alarms to qualifying residents in Martin County.
cards.body:
The Florida Department of Health and Safe Kids Treasure Coast are providing a limited supply of free pool alarms to qualifying residents in Martin County. The initiative aims to add an extra layer of safety for households with residential pools.

Safe Kids Treasure Coast is asking residents to fill out a survey to determine eligibility for the program. The coalition emphasized that a pool alarm is one layer of protection and should always be used alongside close adult supervision, pool barriers and water safety education to help prevent drowning. The alarms are being offered while supplies last, making it important for interested residents to apply promptly.

Residents should be aware that a 9-volt battery is required to operate the alarm but is not included with the free device. This means households receiving an alarm will need to purchase a battery separately before the alarm can be activated and provide protection. The coalition stresses that while pool alarms serve as an important safety tool, they should not replace other critical drowning prevention measures such as constant supervision and proper barriers around pool areas.

For more information about the free pool alarm program or to inquire about eligibility requirements, residents can call 772-462-3501. The partnership between the Florida Department of Health and Safe Kids Treasure Coast reflects ongoing efforts to reduce drowning incidents in the community through increased access to safety equipment and education about water safety practices.

cards.headline: Spain advances to first World Cup final since 2010 with 2-0 win over France
cards.teaser: Mikel Oyarzabal scored from the penalty spot and Pedro Porro added another goal as Spain defeated France 2-0 Tuesday. Spain will face either Argentina or England in the final Sunday in East Rutherford, New Jersey.
cards.body:
Spain advanced to its first World Cup final since winning in 2010 with a 2-0 victory over France on Tuesday. Mikel Oyarzabal scored from the penalty spot in the 22nd minute after teenager Lamine Yamal drew a foul when kicked by defender Lucas Digne. Pedro Porro added a second goal in the 58th minute on a give-and-go with Dani Olmo. A day after his 19th birthday, Yamal was denied a goal on a close offside call that came soon after Porro's score had put Spain up 2-0.

The penalty kick came after a poor first touch with his head left Digne trying to clear the ball when Yamal raced in from behind to challenge in the penalty area. The ball hit off the elbow of the leaping teen before he was kicked by Digne, who was playing in his 63rd game for France only six days before his 33rd birthday. Oyarzabal's fifth goal of this year's World Cup marked the first time either team has trailed in their seven games in this tournament. Spain will face either defending champion Argentina or England on Sunday in East Rutherford, New Jersey. France will play in the third-place game in Miami Gardens, Florida, on Saturday, the day before the final at MetLife Stadium.

cards.headline: Atlanta increases security for England-Argentina World Cup semifinal match
cards.teaser: Atlanta police will increase personnel and resources for Wednesday's England-Argentina World Cup semifinal. The matchup is considered one of the tournament's highest-risk games because of longstanding tensions between the two nations.
cards.body:
Security and police presence will be increased for Wednesday's England-Argentina World Cup semifinal match in Atlanta. Atlanta police said additional personnel and resources are already in place and will continue to be strategically assigned in and around event venues for Wednesday's match. The matchup is considered one of the tournament's highest-risk games because of longstanding tensions between the two nations stemming from the 1982 Falklands War. Videos circulating online appear to show England and Argentina fans clashing in Miami, where England played Norway over the weekend.

Argentina is the defending champion, while England has not won a World Cup since 1966. It is also the first time since England's World Cup win in 1966 that its national team has earned a berth in the semifinals. Argentina has claimed three World Cup titles and has been the tournament's runner-up twice.

cards.headline: Police investigate death of South Africa World Cup player Jayden Adams
cards.teaser: Cape Town police are investigating the death of 25-year-old South Africa World Cup soccer player Jayden Adams. His body was discovered Saturday at a property in Cape Town.
cards.body:
Cape Town central police registered an inquest for investigation following the discovery of the body of a 25-year-old male on Saturday, police said in a statement sent to The Associated Press. Police said the body was discovered at a property in the Cape Town neighborhood of Schotsche Kloof at around 11 a.m. on Saturday. Authorities have not released a cause of death and said circumstances surrounding the incident are under investigation. Adams' father, Juanito Adams, told South African TV news station eNCA on Sunday that the family were waiting for the results of an autopsy and had not yet made any funeral plans. Juanito Adams said it was an untimely death and the family is struggling to process it.

Adams died two weeks after helping South Africa reach the knockout stage of a World Cup for the first time. The 25-year-old played in all three of South Africa's group games as it produced its best performance at the World Cup. He did not feature in the 1-0 loss to Canada in the round of 32 on June 28. South Africa Sports Minister Gayton McKenzie said Adams had played in his team's group game against Czech Republic hours after learning that his grandmother had died. There were moments of silence and tributes for Adams at the England vs. Switzerland World Cup quarterfinal games on Saturday.

cards.headline: England and Argentina renew fierce World Cup rivalry in semifinal
cards.teaser: England and Argentina meet in the World Cup semifinals Wednesday in Atlanta. The winner will play Spain in the final Sunday in East Rutherford, New Jersey.
cards.body:
England and Argentina resume one of the fiercest rivalries in international soccer when they meet in the World Cup semifinals Wednesday in Atlanta. The winner will play Spain in the final Sunday in East Rutherford, New Jersey. England coach Thomas Tuchel said the two shirts are just iconic and the historic matches are iconic. The World Cup rivalry between the nations dates back to 1962, but it was England's 1-0 win in the quarterfinals four years later that saw it intensify. Argentina captain Antonio Rattin, whose death was announced Saturday, was sent off in a bad-tempered match. In 1986 in Mexico, Diego Maradona scored the infamous Hand of God goal that helped Argentina to a 2-1 win in the quarterfinals on the way to becoming world champion for a second time. That game also saw Maradona score what many believe to be the greatest World Cup goal ever when he dribbled the ball from the halfway line before beating England goalkeeper Peter Shilton. Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni said that will be forever in our hearts.

Neither team has had a smooth ride to the semifinals. Argentina survived scares against Cape Verde and Egypt earlier in the knockout rounds and needed extra time to beat 10-man Switzerland 3-1 in the quarterfinals. England had to rally for wins against Congo and Norway after going a goal down. It also endured a physically exhausting game played at altitude, and being down to 10 men, to beat co-host Mexico 3-2 in the round of 16. Lionel Messi has been Argentina's talisman once again, scoring eight goals and also providing crucial assists. England has relied on Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham. Both have six goals so far, with Bellingham scoring twice in each of England's last two games.

cards.headline: World Cup semifinals set with four highest-ranked teams advancing
cards.teaser: The World Cup final four features England, Argentina, France and Spain. Despite underdog success stories and surprise results, the four highest-ranked teams reached the semifinals.
cards.body:
The World Cup semifinals feature the four highest-ranked teams after England and Argentina advanced through the quarterfinals over the weekend. England's Jude Bellingham netted twice to inspire his team past Erling Haaland's Norway. Argentina relied on Julián Alvarez, who scored in extra time to help the team through to the semifinal against Switzerland, though a controversial VAR call also played a role. England has reached this point off the back of two players. Both Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham have scored six goals in the competition. England was last in a World Cup semifinal in 2018 but lost on that occasion to Croatia. The country is looking for its first World Cup title since 1966.

Argentina has relied on Lionel Messi to get out of trouble, though Julián Alvarez was the star in the quarterfinal. Argentina has scored the most goals out of anyone in the competition with 17. The defending champion has the added bonus of experience, with many members of the current squad winning the title back in 2022. France faces Spain in the other semifinal, with France considered by many to be the tournament favorite. Kylian Mbappé has been superb, with his pace and directness proving highly effective. Spain beat France in the semifinals of Euro 2024, a tournament it went on to win, and also beat France in the Nations League last year.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie Opens Registration for Free City University Program
hero.teaser:
Registration is now open for Port St. Lucie City University, a free nine-session program designed to help residents better understand how their local government operates.

Classes
hero.body:
Registration is now open for Port St. Lucie City University, a free nine-session program designed to help residents better understand how their local government operates.

Classes begin Wednesday, Aug. 12, and will be held from **5:30 to 8:30 p.m. in the Council Chambers at Port St. Lucie City Hall**, located at 121 SW Port St. Lucie Blvd.

Participants will learn about City departments, municipal services and the decision-making processes that shape the community. The program also gives residents opportunities to meet City staff, ask questions and gain a closer look at the work involved in operating one of Florida's largest cities.

Residents who complete the course will receive a certificate of completion and may also choose to become a City Ambassador, helping share information about City programs and services throughout the community.

City University is intended to encourage civic engagement while strengthening connections between residents and local government. Since the program began in 2016, more than 600 residents have participated.

**Enrollment is limited to 160 participants.**

Residents who are unable to attend the in-person classes can also access City U on Demand, which offers a more flexible way to learn about Port St. Lucie government and municipal operations.

hero.headline: Vero Beach parents sue city over infant son's remains allegedly disturbed and reburied without consent
hero.teaser: Adam Chrzan and Tanya Crovo allege their infant son's remains were disturbed during maintenance at Crestlawn Cemetery and reinterred without their knowledge.
hero.body:
Adam Chrzan and Tanya Crovo have filed an amended lawsuit against the City of Vero Beach alleging their infant son's remains were disturbed during maintenance work at Crestlawn Cemetery and reburied without their knowledge or consent. The couple's son, identified in court documents only as A.C., died in August 2007 at 37 days old and was buried at the city-owned cemetery. The parents say they did not learn about what allegedly happened until April 2025, nearly 18 years after their son's burial.

According to the complaint, sometime between the 2007 burial and April 2025, heavy equipment being used for maintenance or irrigation work near the burial site breached the grave, damaging or destroying the casket, its contents, and the child's remains. The lawsuit alleges that someone acting in an official capacity for the City of Vero Beach then directed cemetery workers to collect the remains, place them into a new casket, and reinter the child without notifying the parents or obtaining their consent. The amended complaint accuses the city and cemetery of tortious interference with a burial plot and human remains, negligence, negligent infliction of emotional distress, intentional misrepresentation, and fraudulent concealment.

This amended complaint comes after a judge dismissed the family's original lawsuit. The dismissal was not a finding that the allegations were false but rather a ruling that the legal claims as originally pleaded could not proceed against the city under Florida law. The parents have now refiled with different legal arguments in an attempt to overcome the previous dismissal. A judge has not yet ruled on the amended complaint. The City of Vero Beach has declined to comment on the amended complaint.

In court filings responding to the original lawsuit, the city disputed the allegation that irrigation work could have caused the damage described by the parents. The city submitted a survey stating there are no irrigation lines adjacent to the burial plot of A.C. The case highlights the legal protections cities have under Florida law and the challenges families face when seeking accountability for alleged mishandling of cemetery operations. The amended complaint represents the parents' continued effort to hold the city responsible for what they describe as the unauthorized disturbance and reburial of their infant son's remains.
